summary.text: A printing press is a machine that applies pressure to transfer ink onto paper, cloth or a similar material.
The German goldsmith Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type press around 1440, combining four existing technologies into one working system.
Printing brought mass communication to Europe, lowered the cost of printed texts and contributed to the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.

facts.label: Four technologies
facts.value: Screw press, movable type, codex book, mechanized paper

facts.label: His own additions
facts.value: A hand mold for casting type and an oil-based ink

facts.label: Long-lived design
facts.value: The wooden handpress stayed basically the same for over three centuries

items.prompt: Printers in China and in Germany both worked with movable type. Why did it spread widely in only one of those places?

options.label: Rulers there banned woodblock printing outright
A small set of characters made type far cheaper to produce
Paper was available only in one of the regions
Printers there had no machine for applying pressure

items.explain: The Gutenberg press used the Latin alphabet with a relatively small set of characters, while Chinese script needed thousands of characters, making a full set of type costly.

items.prompt: In the 15th century a student wants a textbook, but too few exist. Which condition helped make a printing business workable?

options.label: Copying by hand was slow and costly, so supply fell well short of what readers wanted
Paper was too expensive for any other book trade to survive
Universities had been closing, so fewer people wanted books
Copying by hand had grown fast enough to meet every need

items.explain: The growing number of universities and urban middle class increased demand for books, while hand-copying was slow and expensive.

items.prompt: Farmers had long used a device to squeeze grapes into wine. What part of Gutenberg's invention took its design from it?

options.label: The oil-based ink that stuck to metal type
The codex format that bound the pages together
The mold used for casting each metal letter
The screw press, which applied direct pressure on a flat plane

items.explain: Gutenberg adopted the basic design of the screw press, used for pressing grapes and olives, thereby mechanizing the printing process.

items.prompt: A town's bookshop in 1520 sells more titles in local speech than in Latin. Which change that came with printing fits this?

options.label: Latin had been banned in every printing house of the time
Books increasingly appeared in everyday languages, not Latin
Books stopped being sold and were only lent out by libraries
Presses could print only one language at a time then

items.explain: Books increasingly appeared in vernacular languages rather than Latin, and national languages were standardized.

items.prompt: Why did more adults across Europe learn to read as printing spread?

options.label: Every parish was required to teach reading to adults
Hand-copied books became faster to make than printed ones
Printed texts cost less and were easier to get
Books were made shorter so that they were easier to read

items.explain: The cost of printed texts declined and their availability increased, facilitating higher adult literacy rates across Europe.

items.prompt: The wooden handpress stayed essentially the same for centuries. What finally changed that design?

options.label: The Industrial Revolution, with iron presses and then steam power
The Reformation, which demanded faster Bibles
The invention of movable type in East Asia
The shift from scrolls to the codex

items.explain: The wooden handpress design was largely consistent for over three centuries, until the Industrial Revolution brought the iron press and steam-powered presses.
